title: SQL vs NoSQL
sources: MongoDB, 'NoSQL vs SQL databases' (mongodb.com/resources/basics/databases/nosql-explained/nosql-vs-sql): SQL (relational) databases store data in tables with fixed rows and columns and a predefined schema; NoSQL databases (document, key-value, wide-column, graph) have flexible schemas, and 'NoSQL' is often read as 'not only SQL'

Coursera, 'NoSQL vs SQL Databases' and phoenixNAP 'SQL vs NoSQL': SQL databases usually scale vertically and enforce ACID transactions, which suits financial data; NoSQL databases are typically designed to scale horizontally across many servers

Discord engineering blog, 'How Discord Stores Trillions of Messages' (discord.com/blog/how-discord-stores-trillions-of-messages, 2023): Discord stores trillions of messages in ScyllaDB (a NoSQL wide-column database), migrated from Cassandra
DesignGurus, 'SQL vs NoSQL for system design': many large systems use both (polyglot persistence), choosing per workload

lines.text: but where do we write down every order?
One way is a strict order form,
with the same boxes every single time.
Name, pizza, size, all in neat rows.
That's SQL, a table with a fixed shape,
great for payments, where every number must add up.
lines.caps: GREAT FOR *PAYMENTS | WHERE EVERY *NUMBER | MUST ADD *UP

lines.text: The other way is a notebook,
where every page can look different,
photos on one page, extra toppings on the next.
and easy to spread across lots of servers.
Discord stores trillions of messages like this.
So which one wins? Neither. Big apps use both.
